review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines `DeductivelyEquivalent` (two theories prove the same sentences), `consequence_of_model_inclusion`, `deductivelyEquivalent_of_models_iff`, and the `.mp`/`.mpr` projections. All of these are stated over the vendored Flypitch-style `Fol` framework (`Fol.SentTheory`, `Fol.allRealizeSentence`, `⊢ₛ'`). That framework lives in `LeanPool/NFWeakPartition/Flypitch4/Fol.lean`; it is not Mathlib's `FirstOrder` library. Mathlib's `FirstOrder` has no completeness theorem and no theory-level deductive-equivalence notion for this syntax, so I found no Mathlib, Batteries or core counterpart of the same concept. The file is used in `Equivalence.lean` and `HailperinPresentationBridge.lean`. I also found no competing local definition of the same notion. I checked `DeductivelyEquivalent` only by searching the lean-pool tree and did not do a deep search of Mathlib. The remaining uncertainty is whether Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language.Theory` has an equivalent notion for its own syntax. Even if it does, it would not be an independent replacement here, because the `Fol` types differ.
